title: decision-event v1
description: ONE WRITE-ONCE RECORD OF THE DECISIONS STORE: something that happened to the list of questions waiting for a person. The store is a folder, <HordeHome>\store\decisions\, holding one file per record named by its sequence number in ten digits (0000000007.json). A record is written whole and then given its name once, by a move that the operating system lets exactly one caller win, and is never rewritten or deleted (decisions/Store.ps1). The records in sequence order are the single source of truth: the current list is worked out from them each time (decisions/Rules.ps1) and nothing else is kept. ON DISK: UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, one JSON object. VERSIONING: a reader treats a record that does not match this schema as unreadable and says so by sequence number; it never guesses and never skips it silently. A record that DOES match this envelope and whose kind the reader does not know was written by a later version: it is not damage. It is set aside, reported once for its kind, and costs no question number - the compatibility contract in decisions/Rules.ps1. That contract rests on two promises: question-added is a kind every version knows, and a kind's name never changes meaning. A later kind of event is a new entry in the kind table of decisions/Rules.ps1 and a new definition here; a change to an existing kind's data, or to this envelope, is a v2.

sequence.description: The record's place in the one total order, from 1 with no gaps. It must equal the number in the record's file name.

id.description: The idempotency id the caller chose for the request that made this record: 32 lowercase hex digits. The same id with the same request is answered from this record and writes nothing; the same id with another request is refused.

kind.description: What happened. The closed list is the kind table of decisions/Rules.ps1; each kind's data is a definition below of the same name.

at.description: When the record was written, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z, by the writer's clock. Order is the sequence, never this time.

actor.description: Who made the request, as one lowercase role label (core/roles.json names the roles). WHICH labels may write is not said here: it is the closed list of actors in decisions/Rules.ps1, asked of a request before it is written, so that a new actor is one entry there and not a new version of this schema, and so that a record written under an actor an older version does not list is still read by it.

requestHash.description: SHA-256 of the request as the rules normalised it (operation, actor and what was asked), so that a repost of an id can be told from a reuse of it without comparing whole texts.

data.description: What the kind carries, checked against the definition named for the kind.

number.description: The permanent number the question was given. It is DERIVED, not counted anywhere: the Nth question-added record is question N. It is written down here as a check on that derivation, so that a record which later becomes unreadable cannot shift the number of any question added after it.

changes.description: The fields that change and their new values, schema/decision-question.v1. A field not named keeps its value.

outcome.description: What was done, in plain words. Never blank.

reason.description: Why it is open again, on one line. Never blank.
